references.text: The Israelites ate manna for forty years until they came to a settled land. This verse in Exodus describes the duration of the manna, which ceased when they entered the land of Canaan.
The first account of the manna that God gave the Israelites in the wilderness, the heavenly food that now ceases in Joshua 5:12.
Description of the manna and how the people gathered and prepared it during their journey through the wilderness.
Manna is described as food unknown to both the fathers and the people, given to teach them that man does not live by bread alone.
The Feast of Firstfruits and the harvest of the land's crops, which the Israelites could now enjoy after entering Canaan.
The laws concerning firstfruits and that they were not to eat from the land's produce until the offering was brought, which happened just before the manna ceased.
The psalm recalls how God caused manna to rain down from heaven and gave the people bread of angels.
Nehemiah reminds how God provided them with manna for food and did not withhold it during their journey through the wilderness.
Hebrews mentions the golden jar of manna that was kept in the ark of the covenant as a reminder of God's provision.
Jesus promises to give hidden manna to the one who overcomes, a spiritual parallel to the physical manna that ceased.
Jesus refers to the manna in the wilderness and declares himself the true bread from heaven, in contrast to the temporary manna.
